intro.intro.title: The climate-finance market funders can't see
intro.intro.body: Brazil's Treasury rates every municipality's creditworthiness (CAPAG). CityCatalyst knows each one's emissions and climate risk. Joining the two reveals a fundable pipeline that's invisible today — and ranks it by where a small fix unlocks the most capital.
intro.capag.title: CAPAG — fiscal capacity, A+ to D
intro.capag.body: A Treasury rating built from three indicators: debt, current savings, and liquidity. A+/A/B+/B can borrow with a federal guarantee. C is blocked from that credit channel. D is distressed. n.d. means the city couldn't be rated at all.
intro.graduation.title: Graduation — one fiscal fix from credit
intro.graduation.body: Some CAPAG-C cities already have healthy, grade-A debt — they're blocked only by savings or liquidity. A focused fiscal-management fix graduates them toward CAPAG B and unlocks guaranteed credit. The highest-leverage use of catalytic capital.
intro.gates.title: Unrated & ICF-gated, but fixable
intro.gates.body: n.d. cities are invisible to credit because of a specific Siconfi reporting gap — one accounting fix makes them visible. ICF is Siconfi's accounting-quality ranking, Aicf (best) → Eicf (worst): Aicf earns the '+' upgrade (A→A+), while Dicf/Eicf are ineligible for guaranteed credit on accounting quality alone, regardless of fiscal health. Both gates are cheap to fix — hover any ICF value in the table to see what it means.
intro.use.title: Build a mandate → deployable pipeline
intro.use.body: Tell the tool your instrument, region and climate focus. It returns the cities you can fund, ranked by catalytic leverage. 'Deployable' is real R$ credit headroom (1.2× RCL − debt). Bundle a cohort into one facility, then export the list.

indicator.debt.name: Debt (Endividamento)
indicator.debt.what: Gross consolidated debt ÷ net current revenue. How leveraged the city already is.
indicator.savings.name: Savings (Poupança Corrente)
indicator.savings.what: Current expenses ÷ current revenues, 3-year weighted average. Whether day-to-day operations leave room to invest.
indicator.liquidity.name: Liquidity (Liquidez Relativa)
indicator.liquidity.what: (Cash − short-term obligations) ÷ net current revenue. Whether the city can pay what's due now.
